Rescue operations are ongoing as officials try to determine the number of people potentially trapped under the debris.

articles.title: Kelly Curtis, actress and elder sister of Jamie Lee Curtis, dies at 69 | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: Kelly Curtis, the elder sister of actress Jamie Lee Curtis, passed away at age 69 on Saturday.  She was a talented actress who appeared in films like "Trading Places" and "The Devil's Daughter," as well as television series such as "Star Trek: Deep Space Nine."  Curtis is survived by her husband, playwright Scott Morfee.  Tributes have poured in from colleagues, fans, and members of the entertainment industry.

articles.title: Several feared trapped as five-storey building reduced to rubble in Delhi’s Saket
articles.rephrased_article: A five-storey building collapsed near Saket metro station in south Delhi on Saturday evening, trapping several people under the debris.  The structure housed a coaching institute and construction work was underway on upper floors. Rescue efforts are ongoing with seven fire tenders dispatched to the scene, but authorities have not yet confirmed the number of trapped individuals.

articles.title: Best road trips near Mumbai to take this June for misty hills, beaches, and quick escapes | Destination-of-the-week News - The Indian Express
articles.rephrased_article: Mumbai residents seeking a monsoon escape can consider several road trip options within driving distance. Lonavala, known for its waterfalls and misty views, is a popular choice for spontaneous weekend breaks.  Matheran, India's only automobile-free hill station, offers peaceful retreats with red mud trails and scenic viewpoints. Alibaug provides coastal drives, beaches, and relaxed vacation energy, while Igatpuri boasts lush landscapes and dramatic valley views. Nashik offers vineyard getaways, temple visits, and local food.  For those willing to travel further, the Satara belt presents waterfalls, ghats, and scenic roads.

articles.title: Salman Khan Only Owns One Rolex—But His Real Collection Is Worth Crores
articles.rephrased_article: Salman Khan has a significant watch collection, including a Rolex Rainbow Daytona valued at ₹5.13 crore and a Jacob & Co. "Ram Janmabhoomi" timepiece gifted by his mother. He collaborated with Jacob & Co. to create the "Billionaire III," featuring 714 diamonds, which is a tribute to his father's legacy. The actor has showcased various watches over the years, including a limited-edition "Epic X Ram Janmabhoomi Titanium Edition 2" from Jacob & Co., valued at ₹34 lakhs.

articles.title: Obsession takeover: A Rs 7 crore horror film just exposed Bollywood’s biggest issue - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: A low-budget horror film, "Obsession," directed by Curry Barker and starring Michael Johnston and Inde Navarrette, has become Hollywood's biggest ROI story of 2026.  The film, made for a reported budget of $750,000 to $1 million (roughly Rs 6–8 crore), grossed over $100 million worldwide, earning nearly 80 to 100 times its production cost. This success highlights the shrinking space for mid-budget theatrical films in Bollywood, where studios increasingly prioritize large-scale spectacles and franchise universes.  The film's low-risk, high-concept storytelling model contrasts with the escalating budgets of recent blockbuster releases like "RRR" and "Dhurandhar: The Revenge," which have also achieved significant box office success but rely on massive production costs.

articles.title: Three boys drown in tank in Dharwad taluk - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Three boys, aged 11, 13, and 15, drowned in a village tank in Dharwad taluk on Saturday while swimming. The incident occurred at Kariyammana Kere (Tank) in Singanahalli village.  Police Superintendent Gunjan Arya, Deputy Superintendent of Police Vinod Muktedar, and other officials responded to the scene and recovered the bodies with assistance from expert swimmers.

articles.title: Three boys drown in tank in Dharwad taluk - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Three boys, aged 11, 13, and 15, drowned in a village tank in Dharwad taluk on Saturday. articles.title: The poet who shaped a filmmaker: Vishal Bhardwaj recalls a lifetime of friendship with Bashir Badr
articles.rephrased_article: Vishal Bhardwaj, a renowned filmmaker, mourns the passing of Bashir Badr, a celebrated Urdu poet.  Badr, who died at 91, was known for his profound impact on Bhardwaj's life and career. The two shared a deep bond that began in Meerut, where Bhardwaj was a student and Badr taught. Their friendship spanned decades, during which Bhardwaj learned from Badr's poetry and became a successful filmmaker.  Bhardwaj has honored Badr through his work, including incorporating his poems into films like "Dedh Ishqiya" and composing ghazals based on Badr's verses.  The two remained close even as Bhardwaj's career flourished in Mumbai, with Badr visiting him often and offering encouragement.

articles.title: Naga Chaitanya Approaches Delhi HC Over Defamatory Content Alleging He Cheated On Samantha | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Naga Chaitanya, an actor, has filed a petition in the Delhi High Court against online content and defamatory claims alleging he cheated on his ex-wife Samantha Ruth Prabhu. The actor's legal team argues that unauthorized use of his name, image, and persona across various platforms is damaging his reputation.  Justice Jyoti Singh acknowledged the vulnerability of public figures but stressed limitations to scrutiny. The court will examine Chaitanya's plea for legal protections against such online misuse.

articles.title: Indian student drowned at Wisconsin dam as he jumped to save three friends; feet got stuck in fishing wire - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Anurup Reddy Koduru, a 22-year-old Indian student who recently graduated from the University of North Texas, drowned at Toledo Bend Reservoir on May 29th.  He was swimming with friends when he became entangled in fishing wire and was pulled under water. The incident involved multiple agencies including the South Sabine Fire District, LA Department of Wildlife and Fisheries, North Sabine Fire District, Sabine River Authority, Acadian Ambulance, Life Air Rescue, and the Sabine Parish Sheriff Dive Team. Ashtrith Reddy Koduru, his brother, has set up a fundraiser to help with repatriation and funeral expenses.

articles.title: âHe Was A Magical Human Beingâ: Pooja Bhatt On Her Relationship With Bobby Deol | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Pooja Bhatt reflected on her past relationship with Bobby Deol, calling it a "magical time" in her life.  She emphasized the importance of maintaining dignity and grace, stating that discussing the reasons for their separation would be inappropriate. Deol is currently married to Tanya Deol and has two sons. Pooja Bhatt is married to Manish Makhija, and they separated after 11 years of marriage.

articles.title: Mahima Chaudhry Reacts To Daughter Arinaâs Resemblance To Hollywood Actor Mika Abdalla | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Mahima Chaudhry's daughter, Arina, has been drawing comparisons to Hollywood actor Mika Abdalla.  The resemblance has led to online discussions about Arina potentially making her acting debut. Chaudhry revealed that she has received numerous messages and calls regarding the comparison, finding it flattering. She expressed a desire for her daughter to pursue a career in entertainment.

articles.title: Many Feared Trapped As 5-Storeyed Building Collapses Near Metro Station In South Delhi | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: A five-storey building collapsed in south Delhi's Mehrauli area on Saturday evening, trapping dozens of people under the debris. Rescue teams are working to locate survivors and have so far extricated four individuals alive.  The cause of the collapse is still unknown, but authorities believe it was triggered by a dust storm that swept across Delhi-NCR earlier in the day. Delhi Fire Service personnel responded quickly, calling for reinforcements and cordoning off the area to facilitate rescue efforts.

articles.title: Salary denied for more than 2 years, Olympian judge Bilquis Mir moves CAT
articles.rephrased_article: Bilquis Mir, an Olympian judge and high-profile sports administrator, has filed a contempt case against the Jammu and Kashmir sports department for withholding her salary for over two years.  Mir's legal battle stems from a February order by the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) directing the release of her salary. Despite this, the J-K government has failed to comply with the court's directive, leading to Mir seeking further action through the CAT and High Court. The case highlights the ongoing financial and professional challenges faced by Mir due to bureaucratic delays and raises concerns about the treatment of talented athletes in the region.

articles.title: Building collapses near Saket metro station; 8 persons rescued, several feared trapped - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: An eight-story building collapsed in Saket, Delhi on Saturday evening, trapping several people under the debris. Delhi Fire Services officials responded to the scene and rescued at least eight individuals.  The incident occurred near a tin shed canteen where children were dining, creating panic and prompting a large-scale rescue operation involving multiple agencies including National Disaster Response Force, Delhi Police, and District Disaster Management Authority.

articles.title: Kochi metro worksite accident: SHRC registers suo motu case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: State Human Rights Commission (SHRC) Chairperson Alexander Thomas has requested an investigation by the Ernakulam District Collector into a car accident involving a woman who sustained injuries from an iron piece falling at a Kochi Metro Rail Limited (KMRL) worksite. The Commission seeks information on the incident's cause, the woman's injuries, vehicle damage, compensation status, and KMRL and its contractor's safety measures.  The Collector is expected to submit a report within three weeks, with the Commission requiring both the Managing Director of KMRL and a senior officer representing them to present at a subsequent hearing on July 14th.

articles.title: India’s scientific knowledge predates Persia, brought West out of Stone Age: Jammu and Kashmir Lt. Governor - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Jammu & Kashmir Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha stated that India's knowledge in science, medicine, and astronomy predates Persia and Western countries. He emphasized India's historical role as a center of knowledge for centuries, contributing to global civilization and culture.  Sinha highlighted the Vedic period as a foundation for socio-economic advancement across the world.

articles.title: Youth must believe in their potential, says Sharanbasappa Pappa - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sharanbasappa Pappa, president of the Kalyana Karnataka Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KKCCI), encouraged youth in the region to cultivate self-confidence and determination for success.  He praised the initiative of Adhish Wali, president of the Rotary Club Bidar Silverstar, who organized the two-day Rise Kalyana Karnataka- an Educational Youth Summit 2026. The summit featured a Mega Job Fair with over 50 companies, attracting more than 1,500 students and job aspirants.  Tejasvi Surya, MP for Bengaluru South, delivered a virtual address, alongside entrepreneurs Karan Javali, Swathi Kulkarni, and Anilkumar Bidve.

articles.title: Marcia Lucas: Oscar-winning Star Wars editor dies aged 80
articles.rephrased_article: Marcia Lucas, the Oscar-winning editor of the original Star Wars film, has died at 80 from metastatic cancer.  She was married to George Lucas, the creator of the franchise, and worked on several of his films including *THX 1138* and *American Graffiti*.  Lucas won an Academy Award for Best Film Editing in 1977 for *A New Hope*, and also collaborated with directors like Martin Scorsese on acclaimed films. Her family described her as a "trailblazer" who helped redefine film editing, leaving behind a legacy of emotional intelligence and impactful storytelling.

articles.title: Family pays tribute to girl, 15, who died after swimming at Merseyside beach | Merseyside | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Chiedza Nyanjowa, a 15-year-old from Cheshire, died after struggling in the sea off Merseyside on bank holiday Monday.  She was taken to Alder Hey Children’s hospital and passed away on Saturday.  The incident is one of thirteen fatal water-related incidents during the recent hot weather across England and Wales. The Royal Life Saving Society has issued a warning about cold water shock, urging people to call 999 if they see someone in trouble in the water. A report into Nyanjowa's death has been passed to Sefton coroner’s office.

articles.title: Telangana launches weather advisory initiative to help farmers - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana Agriculture Department launched a weather advisory initiative in partnership with DIL India and Evidence Action, aiming to provide farmers with advance information on rainfall patterns. The program will send alerts via WhatsApp to 17 districts, enabling farmers to make informed decisions regarding agricultural operations such as sowing and irrigation scheduling. Officials believe this technology-driven solution will help minimize crop losses and empower farmers to make better decisions.

articles.title: Animal welfare violations swarm Miami zoo owned by ex-drug kingpin in Tiger King | Miami | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Zoological Wildlife Foundation (ZWF), owned by convicted drug trafficker Mario Tabraue, has been cited for multiple violations of the Animal Welfare Act following botched breeding attempts involving a clouded leopard and a capybara.  The USDA found that the animals were incompatible and injured during an attempt to breed them. The incidents led to the amputation of the female leopard's leg and the death of the capybara. People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (Peta) has called for the closure of ZWF, citing its history of animal welfare violations.

articles.title: Five feared drowned in Tungabhadra at Mantralayam of A.P. - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police are investigating a drowning incident in the Tungabhadra river at Mantralayam, where six relatives, all members of one family, reportedly drowned after misjudging the water depth during a swim.  A rescue operation was launched with expert swimmers and fishermen, but efforts continued late into Saturday night. The victims have been identified as Satish and Yuvan Chandra from Hyderabad, Raghavendra and Dhanu from Mantralayam, and Sandhya from Uravakonda in Anantapur district. One relative, Aparna from Adoni, managed to escape the water.

articles.title: What’s gone wrong at Everyman and can the luxury cinema chain regain its magic? | Travel & leisure | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Everyman, the luxury cinema chain, is facing financial challenges after a quarter-century of success. The company issued a profit warning in December prompting investor concern and leading to the departure of its chief executive and finance director.  The company has struggled with rising competition from rivals like Odeon and Vue, as well as issues stemming from the pandemic and Hollywood strikes. Farah Golant, appointed interim chief executive, is tasked with turning around the business by focusing on paying down debt, optimizing food and beverage sales, and enhancing the membership program.  Analysts believe Everyman has a strong brand and potential to capitalize on the growing movie-going market, especially among younger generations.

articles.title: Korean, Japanese-inspired products drive school stationery trend - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Students across the state are embracing a trend of South Korean and Japanese-inspired stationery, driven by global K-pop influence and digital culture.  The popularity of Kawaii aesthetics, minimalist designs, and pastel colors is particularly strong among younger generations, with many students drawn to functional and aesthetically pleasing items. While some prefer bolder colors and cartoon themes for their school supplies, the overall trend reflects a shift in preferences towards more subtle and modern designs.

articles.title: Future of first Bramley apple tree in doubt as cottage where it stands is sold | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The future of the original Bramley apple tree, planted in Nottinghamshire over 200 years ago by Mary Ann Brailsford, is uncertain after Nottingham Trent University sold the garden where it stands.  Campaigners who sought to preserve the tree as a heritage site are "gobsmacked" by the university's decision, which they believe will reduce its significance and accessibility. The university claims it is supporting the new custodians of the tree with advice on care while also ensuring public access for events.

articles.title: ‘That’s why we work in finance – so one day we can afford air-con’: Britain’s unequal heatwave | London | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: England experienced record-breaking temperatures this week, with London reaching 35C. While some residents in affluent areas like Canary Wharf enjoyed air-conditioned offices and homes, others in deprived areas faced extreme heat in their poorly insulated flats.  Asiyha, a resident of Whitechapel, struggled to sleep due to the high temperatures in her home. Toni, a tech worker, found relief in her newly built flat with air conditioning. Meanwhile, some residents relied on fans and other cooling methods like community gardens for respite from the heat.

articles.title: ‘Maybe it’s because we love the sesh’: how Wales is bucking Britain’s pub-closing trend | Wales | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Despite a national trend of pub closures, the Pig & Swill in Cardiff has seen success since opening.  The new taphouse, co-founded by Lewis Dwyer and Andy Aston, is attracting customers with its focus on quality local produce and its location near popular attractions like Victoria Park. While Wales has bucked the national trend with new pub openings, the hospitality industry overall remains under pressure from rising costs and taxes. David Chapman, executive director of UK Hospitality Cymru, calls for government action to support businesses in the sector.

articles.title: Unruly passenger disrupts United Airlines flight bound for Minneapolis, plane seeks FBI's help - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: United Airlines flight UA2005, en route to Minneapolis from Chicago, was diverted to Dane County Regional Airport in Wisconsin after an unruly passenger attempted to enter the cockpit.  The FBI, along with local law enforcement, responded to the incident and detained the disruptive passenger. The plane landed safely in Madison and passengers resumed their journey to Minneapolis without injuries.

articles.title: Bound by blood: new film highlights Jamaica’s outlawed obeah belief system | Jamaica | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Award-winning Jamaican filmmaker Sosiessia Nixon's new suspense film, *Stew Peas*, explores the enduring belief in obeah, a West African-based spiritual healing tradition. The movie centers on a detective investigating a murder case and uncovering her husband's alleged entanglement with their new maid, who uses menstrual blood to bind him. Producer and actor Ava Eagle Brown believes the film will resonate with Caribbean people worldwide, sparking conversations about the tension between Christianity and obeah.  Cultural studies scholar Sonjah Stanley Niaah welcomes the opportunity to shed light on African spirituality often misunderstood and outlawed by colonial powers. Jamaica's film commissioner Jackie Jacqueline Jackson highlights the importance of showcasing the country's creative industry resilience and its potential for international collaborations.

articles.title: Halal food, Qawwali and live events: Sadiq Khan urges Londoners not to miss Trafalgar Square's Eid celebration - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: London’s Mayor Sadiq Khan highlighted the return of Eid on the Square, a free event celebrating Eid al-Adha, in Trafalgar Square on Saturday, May 30, 2026.  The celebration will feature live performances by various groups, cultural presentations, and family activities like lantern-making and calligraphy workshops. The event aims to showcase London's diverse Muslim communities alongside people of all faiths and backgrounds. Khan emphasized the significance of the event in highlighting the city’s multicultural character and fostering connections between communities.

articles.title: Britons travelling home via EU airports ‘should allow three hours’ before flights | Travel | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Wizz Air boss Yvonne Moynihan advises British passengers returning home via European airports to arrive three hours before their flights due to new security procedures causing long queues. ACI Europe, the European airports association, reports that queues are up to 3.5 hours at peak times and have worsened despite extensive use of partial suspension of the EU entry-exit system (EES). The situation has led to temporary suspensions of EES checks at ports like Dover as authorities seek to alleviate pressure on travelers.

articles.title: Former Kozhikode Mayor and senior CPI(M) leader T.P. Dasan passes away - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: T.P. Dasan, a former Kozhikode Mayor and prominent Communist Party of India (Marxist) leader, has passed away at the age of 76.  He was admitted to a private hospital in Kozhikode city on Friday night after his condition worsened and died on Saturday evening.  Dasan served as the Mayor of Kozhikode from 1992 to 1994 and held other positions within the CPI(M), including chairing the corporation's standing committee on city development. He was also a member of the party’s district secretariat for many years.

articles.title: Thunderstorms, rain likely to continue in Rajasthan for next 4-5 days - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) predicts continued thunderstorms, dust storms, and rain in parts of Rajasthan over the next few days due to a western disturbance.  Areas like Bikaner, Jaipur, Ajmer, Bharatpur, Kota, Jodhpur, and Udaipur are expected to experience strong winds and isolated light to moderate rainfall. The weather office also warned of hailstorms and lightning in some areas. Maximum temperatures are predicted to remain below 44°C, offering relief from the ongoing heatwave.

articles.title: "Your dead husband....": Candace Owens slams Erika Kirk over Charlie Kirk’s private letters, calls fundraising effort “shameless” - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A social media dispute erupted after Candace Owens criticized Erika Kirk for sharing personal letters written by her late husband, Charlie Kirk, on X.  Owens argued that the move was inappropriate and a form of emotional manipulation for fundraising purposes. Supporters of Kirk countered that these posts offered a glimpse into the human side of a public figure and helped preserve Charlie Kirk's legacy. The debate highlights the ongoing tension surrounding the balance between honoring loved ones and respecting privacy in the public sphere.

articles.title: ‘How can you have a Ferrari without any vroom?’: electric model shocks owners’ club | Automotive industry | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ferrari's unveiling of its first fully electric car, the Luce EV, has sparked mixed reactions from fans and industry analysts. While some express skepticism about the design's resemblance to other vehicles, others appreciate the company's effort to appeal to a broader audience beyond traditional petrolhead enthusiasts. The initial financial market response was negative, with stock prices dropping, but CEO Benedetto Vigna claims interest is growing among potential buyers.  Despite the backlash, Ferrari remains confident in its vision for the Luce and its ability to capture a niche market of open-minded wealthy buyers.

articles.title: Washington state crews find body of another victim in paper mill explosion | Washington state | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Nippon Dynawave Packaging Company in Longview, Washington experienced a massive chemical tank rupture on Tuesday, resulting in the death of nine workers and leaving two unaccounted for. The incident caused severe burns and lung damage from the release of white liquor, a caustic chemical used to break down wood.  Crews have recovered six bodies and are working to identify them while decontaminating the area. Nippon Paper Group, the company's parent organization, offered condolences to the families of those who perished.

articles.title: Off Campus: Why ice hockey romances are TV's hottest genre
articles.rephrased_article: The popularity of ice hockey romance adaptations has surged, with Amazon Prime's "Off Campus" becoming a global phenomenon. Based on author Elle Kennedy's books, the show follows college ice hockey players and their romantic entanglements, praised for its portrayal of female desire, emotionally intelligent male characters, and high-stakes sports action.  The series has garnered praise from fans for its respectful treatment of women, tackling sensitive topics like sexual assault and domestic violence while showcasing the emotional intelligence of its male characters. Content creators and viewers alike have lauded the show's nuanced approach to hockey romance, highlighting its ability to engage audiences beyond typical stereotypes associated with the genre.

articles.title: Punjab lawyers unhappy with lacunae in biometric system - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Lahore High Court (LHC) has faced criticism from the legal fraternity for its mandatory biometric verification system, which they claim is disproportionately impacting access to justice.  Lawyers argue that technical glitches and a "pay-to-access" model are creating unnecessary obstacles, particularly for vulnerable litigants. The Pakistan Bar Council and Punjab Bar Council, along with the LHC administration committee, were consulted before implementing the system, but lawyers contend they were not adequately involved in its design.  The Lahore Bar Association (LBA) has issued an ultimatum to the LHC, demanding a rationalization of the biometric verification requirement.

articles.title: Portion of platform shed collapses at Lucknow station, three injured - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Three individuals, including a traveling ticket examiner (TTE) and two passengers, were injured when a portion of a platform shed collapsed at Lucknow Junction Railway Station. The incident occurred around 8:15 a.m. on platform number five, prompting panic among commuters.  Railway Protection Force (RPF), Government Railway Police (GRP), and railway officials rescued the injured after removing the collapsed structure. Divisional Railway Manager (DRM) Sunil Kumar Verma visited the hospital and ordered an inquiry into the incident, promising strict action against responsible parties.

articles.title: Vivid Sydney cancels all drone shows after 83 drones plunged into Darling Harbour | Vivid festival | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Vivid Sydney has cancelled all remaining drone shows after 83 drones fell from the sky into Darling Harbour this week, prompting a full assessment of the aerial light show. The incident occurred on Monday during a performance called Star-Bound, with an "unforeseen change in the radio frequency environment" causing the drones to malfunction and fall into the water. Skymagic, the UK-based operator of the drone show, is investigating all possibilities but assured the public that no one was at risk.  Vivid Sydney has replaced the drone shows with fireworks displays and will continue until June 13th.

articles.title: Action initiated against five temple staff for demanding money from devotees in Tiruchendur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Minister for Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) S. Ramesh conducted a surprise inspection at the Subramanya Swami Temple in Tiruchendur, revealing irregularities in darshan arrangements and money collection from devotees. Temple Joint Commissioner K. Ramu issued orders barring temple priest G. Ayappan from performing kainkaryam duties, removing security personnel K. Karuppasamy and A. Thoppu from duty, and suspending two tonsure workers, P. Sankar and V. Nagaraj, for receiving bribes.  The Minister clarified that an explanatory letter was received from the individual involved in the irregularities but no apology was given.

articles.title: The ghost in the machine is real: How physicists finally tracked down the hidden force disrupting CERN's most powerful accelerator | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Physicists at CERN and the GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research have mapped a previously unobserved resonance structure within the Super Proton Synchrotron (SPS), a four-mile-long accelerator.  The discovery, confirmed by simulations and experimental data, was made possible after two decades of research into particle losses in the SPS. This mapping will help improve beam quality for future high-energy colliders like the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) and contribute to advancements in fusion energy research. The structure's existence was predicted years ago but its precise nature remained elusive until now, paving the way for further research on how to mitigate its effects and optimize particle accelerator performance.

articles.title: Meet the Moon Trees: Apollo 14 astronaut carried hundreds of tree seeds around the Moon in 1971 and now they are flourishing across America | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: NASA and the US Forest Service collaborated on a pioneering spaceflight experiment during the Apollo 14 mission in 1971.  Astronaut Stuart Roosa carried hundreds of tree seeds into lunar orbit, where they experienced launch, deep-space travel, lunar orbit, and re-entry. The seeds survived these challenges and were later successfully germinated, creating what became known as "Moon Trees." These trees are now found in parks, schools, courthouses, universities, and government sites across the United States, serving as living reminders of one of NASA's most unusual and enduring spaceflight experiments.

articles.title: New complaint from reinstated employee adds to AMMA row - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A woman employee of the Association of Malayalam Movie Artists (AMMA), Athulya P., filed a fresh complaint against three AMMA office-bearers - Cuckoo Parameswaran, Unni Shivapal, and Neena Kurup - alleging workplace harassment, conspiracy, and character assassination.  She previously lodged two separate complaints with the police regarding her alleged illegal termination from service at the AMMA office but the police have not registered cases. Athulya P., who was reinstated following an executive committee decision on May 12, claims these individuals continued to target her after the reinstatement.

articles.title: “No dignity”: Matt Walsh erupts over Erika Kirk boyfriend rumor while Blake Wynn breaks silence - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Matt Walsh strongly defended Erika Kirk, the widow of late Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk, against allegations that she is romantically involved with Blake Wynn.  The claims originated from an X account called Project Constitution, which alleged Erika Kirk was seen at a Beverly Hills hotel with Wynn and had been "moving on" since her husband's death. Erika Kirk and Blake Wynn both denied the accusations, with Erika Kirk stating that she was celebrating her son's birthday in Arizona on May 14th and that Wynn is engaged to his longtime girlfriend.  The online dispute has attracted significant attention across social media platforms.

articles.title: Dabbawalas: The men who fed Mumbai - and are slowly disappearing
articles.rephrased_article: The dabbawala system, a centuries-old tradition of delivering home-cooked meals in Mumbai, is facing challenges due to the shift towards remote work. The pandemic disrupted daily deliveries as offices closed and people began working from home. While some dabbawalas have adapted by taking on additional jobs, the number of registered workers has fallen significantly.  The system's future remains uncertain as younger generations are opting for higher-paying jobs or starting their own businesses, leaving the traditional trade struggling to survive.

articles.title: After decades risking arrest, South Korea's tattooists are stepping into the limelight
articles.rephrased_article: South Korea's top court overturned its 1992 ruling that defined tattooing as a medical act, ending decades of legal battles by tattoo artists. This decision allows for the profession to operate legally and openly. The move comes after years of advocacy from tattooists, who faced harassment and fines for operating without licenses.  The celebration of body art, known as Ink Bomb, was held in Seoul with over 90 local tattooists and artists participating. Despite the recent legal victory, some challenges remain, including social stigma and ongoing trials against prominent tattoo artists.

articles.title: DJ Akademiks spots bigger problem in Clavicular and DaBaby nightclub confrontation caught on video - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A public disagreement between streamer Clavicular and rapper DaBaby at a Miami nightclub escalated after Clavicular attempted to stop DaBaby's performance due to alleged firearm violations.  DJ Akademiks, who was streaming the event, warned Clavicular about dealing with established artists differently than internet personalities. Akademiks stated that DaBaby is a "bad man" and suggested that attempting to remove him from the stage would be futile. The incident occurred after Clavicular faced legal trouble in Florida for a firearm incident involving an alligator.

articles.title: Who is Allen Ferrell? YouTuber banned for life from Cedar Point and all Six Flags parks over chicken nugget stunt - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Allen Ferrell, a U.S.-based YouTuber, has been banned from all Six Flags parks for life after filming himself eating chicken nuggets while riding the Millennium Force roller coaster in Ohio.  The incident, which went viral online, violated Cedar Point's safety rules prohibiting loose items on rides, including food. The park stated that Ferrell’s actions posed a risk to riders and others nearby. While Ferrell acknowledged the seriousness of his actions, he expressed disappointment over the ban and maintained that the challenge was fun.

articles.title: ‘Culture of silence’ blamed for surge in violence against women - Newspaper - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Human rights advocates, legal experts, and civil society leaders in Sukkur called for an overhaul of the justice system to combat gender-based violence. They emphasized that legislation alone is insufficient without a change in public mindset and state accountability, citing systemic failures within law enforcement and the judiciary as major obstacles.  The speakers highlighted the "culture of silence" fueled by social pressure and stigma, preventing victims from reporting abuse. The event concluded with a joint resolution demanding stringent institutional accountability, immediate enforcement of existing laws, and a unified campaign to eradicate violence against women and girls in the province.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Euripides: “For in other ways a woman is full of fear, defenseless, dreads the sight of cold steel; but, when once she…” | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Euripides' quote, "For in other ways a woman is full of fear, defenseless, dreads the sight of cold steel; but, when once she is wronged in the matter of love, no other soul can hold so many thoughts of blood," explores the emotional transformation that heartbreak can cause. The quote highlights how betrayal can awaken anger and resentment in individuals who were previously gentle or fearful, emphasizing the unpredictable nature of emotional responses to betrayal.  This psychological observation resonates with modern experiences, as people often struggle with lasting emotional scars after experiencing betrayal in relationships.

articles.title: Youtuber Sued: YouTuber sued by Ontario Tech University after allegedly throwing curry at students during prank - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ontario Tech University has filed a lawsuit against content creator Fique Ayub, alleging he disrupted classes and threw curry at students during prank videos on its Oshawa campus. The university claims Ayub entered lecture halls without permission, interfered with lessons, and caused damage to property. Ayub, who denies the allegations, argues his videos are satirical comedy and that he is not profiting from them.  The lawsuit seeks damages for disruption and unauthorized filming on university property.

articles.title: Twitch Streamer Asmongold: “This is getting bad guys”: Twitch streamer Asmongold reflects on being 36, single, and isolated - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Twitch influencer Asmongold, whose real name is Zack Hoyt, went viral after sharing a vulnerable video on his live stream.  He discussed feeling lonely and stuck in a repetitive daily routine, prompting viewers to express concern and offer support. The clip sparked conversations about the negative effects of isolation, particularly within the online world. Asmongold, who has been single since 2019, is known for discussing mental health issues and personal hardships on his platform.  His honest words have resonated with many viewers.

articles.title: Delhi High Court upholds TRAI regulations capping television ads to 12 minutes per hour - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Delhi High Court upheld the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India’s (TRAI) regulations capping television advertisements at 12 minutes per clock hour, rejecting petitions from broadcasters and news channels. The court ruled that TRAI acted within its statutory powers by introducing the cap in 2013, citing consumer complaints and concerns about excessive commercial interruptions impacting viewing experience.  The court acknowledged that while television operates differently than print media, the time-bound nature of broadcasting necessitates regulation to ensure a fair and reasonable viewing experience for consumers.

articles.title: Meet Tesh Jennings, an Indian-American rancher who says 'not all Indians code' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: An Indian-American cowboy named Tesh Jennings gained notoriety after a video showcasing his ranch life went viral.  The video, which showed him working cattle and growing food, sparked controversy as some users expressed racist comments, while others praised his assimilation and called him "more American than Americans." Jennings responded by emphasizing that he simply pursued his dream of ranching and the hate has only motivated him to work harder. He is seeking funding to expand his ranch.

articles.title: Heat wave to ease from Sunday as rain likely in parts of Andhra Pradesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) and the A.P. State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) predict a gradual decline in temperatures across Andhra Pradesh starting Sunday, but severe heat conditions are expected to persist on Saturday, particularly in Polavaram, Kakinada, Eluru, and Krishna districts.  Temperatures reached 45°C to 46°C in these areas, with the highest recorded at Kommipadu in SPSR Nellore district. While some locations received light rainfall, others experienced strong winds that caused minor damage in Vijayawada and surrounding areas. The IMD forecasts isolated heavy rain and thunderstorms over South Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema on May 30 and 31.

articles.title: 'Controversial' Korea setting for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4
articles.rephrased_article: Infinity Ward, the developer of the popular Call of Duty franchise, announced its latest installment, Modern Warfare 4, featuring a campaign set in a fictionalized renewed conflict on the Korean Peninsula. The game will focus on South Korean soldiers battling a full-scale North Korean invasion and includes fan-favorite Captain Price. While some Koreans have embraced the inclusion of their country's military in the game, others expressed concerns about potential controversy surrounding the portrayal of the ongoing inter-Korean conflict. Dr. Sarah Son, a Senior Lecturer in Korean Studies at the University of Sheffield, noted that while such conflicts are often depicted from a South Korean perspective, this could be viewed differently by a global audience.

articles.title: Telangana Information Commission clears massive backlog - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana State Information Commission (TGIC) has disposed of 14,434 cases since its formation in May 2025, leaving 10,996 pending. The commission has processed nearly 1,200 cases per month and interacted with over 30,000 individuals involved in the RTI process during hearings.  State Chief Information Commissioner (RTI) Chandrasekhar Reddy, along with other commissioners, briefed Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy on the commission's activities and functioning. The commission also conducted awareness camps and completed an expenditure audit for the first time since its inception.

articles.title: 'Wish me happy birthday': Indian-origin woman falls from bridge during vacation in Mexico, shares harrowing experience - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nina Bakhshi, an Indian-origin Californian makeup artist, suffered severe injuries after falling from a bridge at Cenote La Noria in Mexico during a guided ATV tour. She was left stranded for over an hour without medical assistance and required emergency surgery due to her lack of travel insurance. Bakhshi  launched a fundraiser to cover the cost of her treatment and recovery, which is ongoing as she continues to face physical therapy, follow-up appointments, and other expenses.

articles.title: ‘Flybrary’ to come up soon at Mysuru airport - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mysuru airport and the Rotary Club of Mysore West are collaborating to establish a "Flybrary" in the Security Hold area. The initiative aims to promote reading among air travelers and enhance passenger engagement at the airport. A book handover program was held on Friday, with representatives from the Rotary Club handing over books for the Flybrary's collection. Airport director P. V. Usha Kumari and other stakeholders were present at the event.

articles.title: Two killed, 35 injured as sleeper bus rams truck on Agra-Lucknow Expressway - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A sleeper bus carrying 70 passengers collided with a rice-laden truck on the Agra-Lucknow Expressway in Uttar Pradesh, resulting in the deaths of driver Ram Jeevan (43) and passenger Ram Naresh (35). The accident occurred near milestone 83 under Karhal police station limits, leaving 35 passengers injured.  Police are investigating the cause of the crash, which involved the bus rear-ending the truck.

articles.title: Ronan Androgenic: Why ‘Looksmaxxing’ streamer Androgenic got kicked off a Jetstar flight despite claiming medical clearance? - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ronan Androgenic, a 25-year-old Australian influencer known for promoting "looksmaxxing," was removed from a Jetstar flight after airline staff expressed concerns about his physical condition following facial surgery.  Androgenic, who claimed he had medical clearance to fly, disputed the decision and argued that his tiredness was due to preparing for sleep. Jetstar stated that crew members are trained to assess passenger fitness to fly and can refuse travel if they deem someone unfit.

articles.title: Milan gives bull mosaic testicles worn down by spinning tourists some TLC
articles.rephrased_article: Milan's city council is restoring a famous bull mosaic in the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II arcade after tourists have worn down its delicate tiles by performing a tradition involving grinding heels on the bull's testicles. The restoration, which began this week, aims to return the artwork to its former glory and address the damage caused by the popular ritual.  Artisan Gianluca Galli is working to cut new pieces of stone by hand as onlookers watch.

articles.title: KPMG Australia’s CEO Andrew Yates quits over whistleblower scandal | KPMG | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: KPMG’s Australian chief, Andrew Yates, resigned immediately following the firm's failure to properly respond to whistleblower allegations regarding the misuse of client information. KPMG’s chair, Martin Sheppard, apologized unreservedly to the whistleblower and acknowledged that internal reviews fell short of expectations. The head of KPMG’s audit and assurance division, Julian McPherson, also stepped down, while Senator Deborah O’Neill, who first revealed the allegations, called for an investigation into the firm's conduct by the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (Asic).  The Asic is conducting a preliminary investigation into three individuals at KPMG, not the firm itself.

articles.title: Anthropic soars to $965bn valuation, leapfrogging OpenAI | Technology News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Anthropic, the maker of the Claude family of chatbots, has surpassed OpenAI in valuation, reaching a $965 billion figure after raising $65 billion from private investors.  The funding round, led by Altimeter Capital, Greenoaks, Dragoneer and Sequoia Capital, will support Anthropic's growth and research efforts. CEO Dario Amodei stated that the funds will be used to meet the high demand for Claude and bring it to more workplaces. Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner highlighted the adoption of Claude by demanding organizations as evidence of Anthropic's leadership in AI innovation.

articles.title: CMAT shares ‘deep sadness’ over body-shaming after BBC Radio 1 Big Weekend performance | CMAT | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: CMAT, an Irish singer-songwriter, addressed online abuse she has received following her appearance at BBC’s Radio 1 Big Weekend. She criticized the disparity in treatment towards herself and other female musicians on the lineup, comparing the experiences of Zara Larsson and Olivia Dean to hers.  CMAT stated that despite her success, she is subjected to body shaming and feels compelled to defend herself against online negativity. The singer-songwriter has previously addressed similar issues with her music.

articles.title: "Attacking Erika IS attacking Charlie": Candace Owens drags Charlie Kirk’s old support into escalating online firestorm - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A resurfaced video of Charlie Kirk publicly supporting Candace Owens has reignited controversy surrounding their relationship and the conservative commentator's legacy. The clip, filmed years ago, resurfaced amidst heightened tensions following Kirk's death and Owens' recent public statements about his family and Turning Point USA.  While some users praised the friendship shown in the video, others criticized Owens for her actions and questioned her loyalty to Kirk.

articles.title: "I'm done with the abuse": QTCinderella threatens legal action against “hate farming” clip accounts after emotional return online - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: QTCinderella, a popular Twitch streamer, has announced plans to pursue legal action against accounts that she believes are profiting from the unauthorized use of her content.  She claims these accounts have been twisting harmless moments from her broadcasts into fuel for targeted online attacks and is taking steps to defend herself against what she describes as coordinated hate campaigns. QTCinderella's decision has garnered support from fans and fellow creators who have expressed concerns about the growing problem of clip farming on streaming platforms and social media, where misinformation and sensationalized content are often used to drive engagement.

articles.title: Preparation, not fear will combat El Nino: Agriculture Minister Chouhan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan announced that the Ministry of Agriculture is preparing advisories for farmers on appropriate crops to grow in regions expected to experience insufficient monsoon rains due to El Nino predictions. The India Meteorological Department has not yet issued a final prediction, but the ministry is already assessing potential impacts and developing contingency plans.

articles.title: Indians fill out every form without blinking: CEO says Americans are not lazy, they have low tolerance for meaningless paperwork - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: John Konrad, CEO of gCaptain, argues that the issue is not with Indian visa holders, but rather the US bureaucratic system. He states that Indians are accustomed to navigating complex processes and paperwork in India, making them more adept at dealing with it than Americans who often quit before completing tedious tasks.  He believes the real problem lies in the current system, which rewards those skilled at navigating bureaucracy while hindering others.

articles.title: ‘Reinforcing stereotypes’: Row over Indian tourists doing Garba on Vietnam airport tarmac in viral video - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Indian tourists sparked debate online after a video showed them performing Garba on an airport tarmac in Vietnam.  The clip, shared widely across social media platforms, drew criticism for the inappropriate location and potential safety risks associated with dancing near an aircraft. While some praised the group for celebrating Indian culture abroad, others expressed concern about the behavior's impact on public decorum and potential negative stereotypes about Indian tourists.

articles.title: Farmer’s sudden death left 1,400 acres unharvested, then 75 neighbours arrived and harvested everything for his family | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: After Randy Fyllesvold, a North Dakota farmer, died unexpectedly in September 2025, his family faced the daunting task of harvesting 1,400 acres of unharvested corn and soybeans.  Wyatt Thompson and Andy Gates, close friends of the deceased, rallied neighboring farmers to help bring in the crops, resulting in a coordinated community effort that saw over 75 farmers arrive with equipment and trucks. The volunteer operation, which resembled a professional harvest, took place over two days, demonstrating the strong bonds within rural farming communities and highlighting the importance of neighborly support during times of crisis.  The story quickly spread across the country, inspiring many to reflect on the power of collective kindness and solidarity in difficult times.

articles.title: PDS rice laden lorry overturns on hill road near Gudiyatham - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A  lorry carrying 35 tonnes of PDS rice overturned on a hill road in Paradarami village near Gudiyatham, Tamil Nadu. The driver, G. Sivakumar, lost control of the vehicle after encountering wet and slippery conditions caused by recent rainfall.  The driver was injured and treated at the Government Taluk Hospital in Gudiyatham. Police inspected the scene and lifted the overturned lorry to a safer location.

articles.title: Clavicular Miami Nightclub Incident: Why streamer Clavicular suddenly tried removing DaBaby from his Miami club mid-performance - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Clavicular, a popular streamer, became embroiled in a public confrontation with rapper DaBaby at his Miami nightclub, Bacara.  Videos show Clavicular yelling for DaBaby to leave the stage while the rapper continued performing despite the streamer's demands. The incident stemmed from reports that members of DaBaby's crew allegedly brought firearms into the club, violating Bacara's strict no-firearm policy. While the situation escalated online, DaBaby has not publicly addressed it and there are no reports of injuries or police involvement.

articles.title: Victorian greyhound trainer avoids ban despite dog being found with cocaine in system | Victoria | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Greyhound trainer Geoffrey Dalton avoided a temporary ban despite his dog testing positive for cocaine before a race. The Victorian Civil and Administrative Tribunal (Vcat) ruled against the state regulator, Greyhound Racing Victoria (GRV), who had appealed a nine-month disqualification imposed by the Victorian Racing Tribunal (VRT). Vcat determined that Dalton's suspension was "harsh" because he had let his registration lapse and that the case did not warrant an active ban.  The decision acknowledged Dalton's long career in greyhound racing but emphasized the seriousness of prohibited substance use in the industry.

articles.title: Oldest evidence of human cremation discovered: Burned 100,000-year-old Homo sapiens bones found in Ethiopia’s Afar Rift | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: In the Afar Rift of Ethiopia, researchers are studying ancient bones dating back 100,000 years that show signs of intense heat and unusual post-mortem treatment.  Scientists at the University of Oulu suggest these burn marks could indicate early human cremation practices, but other possibilities remain under consideration. The site also reveals evidence of animal remains and stone tools suggesting a seasonal floodplain environment where early humans likely moved frequently and adapted to changing resources. While the significance of the findings is still being debated, they raise questions about how early humans in East Africa dealt with death, fire, and memory.

articles.title: CNN sues Perplexity, alleging unlawful distribution of copyrighted content | Media News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: CNN has filed a lawsuit against Perplexity, alleging the AI search engine provider unlawfully distributed its copyrighted content. The complaint claims that Perplexity copied thousands of CNN stories, videos, and images to power its products, resulting in "identical or substantially similar" competing content.  CNN is seeking unspecified monetary damages and a court order preventing further violations of its intellectual property rights.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Canadian-American psychologist Albert Bandura: “Where everyone is responsible, no one is really responsible” | - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Albert Bandura, a renowned psychologist, warned that shared responsibility can weaken accountability. His quote, "Where everyone is responsible, no one is really responsible," highlights the tendency for individuals to assume someone else will address problems in groups like workplaces, schools, and online communities. This diffusion of responsibility often leads to inaction because people mentally distance themselves from taking ownership. Bandura's work on social learning theory emphasizes how observing others' behavior shapes our own actions, suggesting that collective passivity can become normalized when individuals repeatedly see a lack of accountability.  This phenomenon is evident in modern workplaces where unclear roles and communication breakdowns lead to inaction despite widespread awareness of issues.

articles.title: Inside court as Matthew Perry's assistant was sentenced
articles.rephrased_article: Kenneth Iwamasa, the live-in personal assistant to actor Matthew Perry, was sentenced to 41 months in prison for injecting the actor with ketamine. Iwamasa, who had no medical training, worked with two doctors to provide Perry with over $50,000 worth of the drug in the weeks leading up to Perry's death. The incident occurred in October 2023 in Los Angeles, where Perry was found dead in his backyard hot tub.

articles.title: ‘I felt my humanity was bastardised’: Cynthia Erivo says reaction to Ariana Grande red carpet incident rooted in racism | Movies | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Cynthia Erivo and Ariana Grande were startled when a man, Johnson Wen, jumped a barrier at the Singapore premiere of "Wicked: For Good" and rushed towards them.  Erivo intervened to remove Wen from the situation, stating that personal space is important, regardless of who you are. The incident sparked social media discussion about Erivo's physique and her role in protecting Grande. Erivo expressed discomfort with these assumptions and decided not to campaign for Oscars for the film.

articles.title: Florida influencer with no right hand gets ticket for using phone in ‘right hand’ while driving - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Katie, an adaptive athlete known online as “Slightlyoff.balance,” had a traffic ticket for using her right hand while driving dismissed in Florida after the officer who issued it requested its dismissal before the court hearing. Katie shared details of the incident on social media, where many users encouraged her to challenge the citation. The case was dropped due to "lack of evidence."

articles.title: Justice Babar Sattar decides to retain official residence in Islamabad - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Justice Babar Sattar, transferred from the Islamabad High Court (IHC) to the Peshawar High Court (PHC), has decided to continue residing in his Islamabad F-6 sector residence during his tenure in Peshawar.  Sources say he formally requested retention of the accommodation, citing Presidential Order 1997 which allows judges to retain one official residence. The issue of judicial accommodation for IHC judges remains contentious due to limited availability of Category-I residences. A landmark judgement by Justice Sattar in 2023 clarified that judges are entitled to official accommodation from their appointment date and throughout their service, impacting the judiciary's independence.

articles.title: Art in conflict zones: Nicky Chandam’s visual documentation of Manipur and the politics of performance - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nicky Chandam, a photographer from the Northeast, presents her exhibition "Manipur & Archives: A Visual Documentation of Live Art Over a Decade" in Chennai. The exhibition showcases 58 photographs capturing Manipuri performance cultures across Delhi and Imphal from 2011 to 2025.  The exhibition features works by renowned artists like Astad Deboo, Mamata Shankar, and Ratan Thiyam, alongside emerging talents, and highlights the impact of conflict on artistic expression in Manipur. The exhibition runs through May 31st at Alliance Française Madras.

articles.title: CM Vijay’s signature suit: Has Tamil Nadu’s new Chief Minister sparked a blazer trend? - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: C Joseph Vijay, the new Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu, has made a bold fashion statement by consistently wearing blazers instead of traditional white shirts and veshtis.  Inspired by a viral shopping offer advertising a "CM Vijay Look" for ₹3,999, some are considering adopting this style, though it comes with a significant price tag.

articles.title: "Superman to Clark Kent": Clavicular heavily trolled after quitting testosterone as viral transformation shocks viewers - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Clavicular, a 20-year-old influencer known for his looksmaxxing content, has sparked debate after appearing noticeably different during a recent livestream following a decision to stop using testosterone and other substances. Some viewers mocked his new look while others praised him for prioritizing long-term health over social media approval. The influencer's transformation highlights the pressures of online beauty culture and raises questions about the impact of performance-enhancing drugs on both physical appearance and mental well-being.

articles.title: Morning flight from Bengaluru to Kalaburagi by Star Air starting June 10 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Star Air has revised the flight timings for its Kalaburagi-Bengaluru route, shifting from evening operations to a morning schedule. The new schedule will see flights departing Bengaluru at 6:30 a.m. and arriving in Kalaburagi at 7:40 a.m., with return flights leaving at 8:10 a.m. and reaching Bengaluru at 9:20 a.m. The Kalyana Karnataka Chamber of Commerce and Industry (KKCCI), which had requested the change, hopes for future expansion of flight frequencies and connectivity under the UDAN scheme.

articles.title: Paul McCartney on playing guitar with Paul Mescal: 'He knew it better than I did!'
articles.rephrased_article: Paul McCartney recently released his new album, "The Boys of Dungeon Lane," which features songs inspired by his childhood in Liverpool. The album explores themes of family, music, and the Beatles' legacy. McCartney has been collaborating with other artists, including actor Paul Mescal, who is set to portray him in a forthcoming biopic.  He also discussed his upcoming plans for a Beatles museum in London and expressed interest in hologram technology used in recent Abba concerts.

articles.title: Is 'out of control' US tipping culture spreading overseas?
articles.rephrased_article: The debate about tipping culture in the US is spreading internationally, with some countries seeing increased pressure to tip from American tourists.  Efling Union, a union in Iceland, reports that American visitors are prompting restaurants to ask for gratuities, which has angered locals who view it as an unnecessary surcharge on already high prices. In Mexico City, local residents blame American tourists for the growth of tipping culture. SumUp, a manufacturer of card readers, notes that UK cafes and restaurants have increased their use of digital tip prompts by 78% since 2022.  Michael Lynn, author of "The Psychology of Tipping," attributes the rise in tipping globally to digital payment machines prompting customers to add tips. Lillian Price, an animal care worker in Philadelphia, believes that tipping is becoming excessive and unnecessary in other locations.

articles.title: Crew, commuters injured after SETC bus plunges into pit near Ambur - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A SETC bus carrying 46 passengers, including women and children, plunged into a roadside pit on the Chennai-Bengaluru Highway in Tirupattur, injuring both the bus crew and commuters. The incident occurred around 2:30 am when driver G. Selva Murugan lost control of the vehicle.

articles.title: How my brother went from liberal Hollywood actor to manosphere 'messiah'
articles.rephrased_article: Luis Castilleja, known online as El Temach, has transformed from a Hollywood actor to a prominent manosphere influencer. His content, which promotes misogynistic and hyper-masculine views, has gained him millions of followers in Latin America and beyond.  This trend is fueled by the rise of Western influencers like Andrew Tate who have capitalized on men's frustrations with perceived societal changes. A BBC investigation found that these influencers are monetizing their platforms through merchandise sales, YouTube "Super Chats," and workshops. The impact of this content is evident in the lives of young men, such as Julián, who initially sought self-improvement but became consumed by misogynistic narratives.  El Temach's content has also been linked to real-world consequences, including controlling behavior and violence against women.

articles.title: Matthew Perry's assistant jailed for 41 months over actor's ketamine death
articles.rephrased_article: Kenneth Iwamasa, Matthew Perry's assistant, was sentenced to 41 months in prison for his role in the actor's death. Iwamasa admitted to injecting Perry with ketamine and concealing evidence after the actor's passing. Prosecutors sought a three-year and five-month sentence, while Iwamasa's attorney argued that he acted at Perry’s direction. The case involved multiple defendants who supplied ketamine to Perry, exploiting his addiction for profit.

articles.title: Reuters executive Simon Robinson expected to replace Justin Stevens as ABC news director | Australian Broadcasting Corporation | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Simon Robinson, currently deputy to the editor-in-chief of Reuters, is expected to be appointed as news director of the ABC in coming days.  He will replace Justin Stevens, who resigned after four years, citing personal and professional reasons. Hugh Marks, managing director of the ABC, stated that Stevens felt it was time for a refresh and rejuvenation of the organization's output. The appointment comes as the ABC seeks to adapt to the changing media landscape.
